Enstar, the gas utility for almost half of Alaska's population, publishes a tariff section numbered 1200 and titled Interruption.

Cook Inlet storage read 7.65 of 13.0 Bcf on September 10th, or 58.8 percent of design. Enstar says any reductions would be phased by customer class under that tariff, with facilities serving human needs and occupancy ranked highest.

The public learns where a large commercial and industrial load sits only because Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt told his city council what Enstar described to Southcentral mayors on August 21st.

A 36 cell grid of the daily readings with the 2 unverified days left empty, and the tariff volume drawn end on with only its top step marked.

Should the order of cuts be public before the next large load is sited?

#CookInletGas #UtilityTariffs #SouthcentralAlaska

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

One limit worth stating. The text of Section 1200 did not extract, so nothing here claims to have read it. What the section is called comes from Enstar's own tariff page. Where a large commercial and industrial load sits in the order comes from Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt's account to his city council of what Enstar described to Southcentral mayors on August 21st.

Editor's note

Raw craft 8.47 is this deck's highest. The four scoring passes are in the record because the run iterated against each one rather than arguing with it, which is what a below-threshold score is for.
The deck's spine changed twice and got better both times. At the claims gate the original thesis died: there is no published tariff text ranking large commercial ahead of residential. What survived is sharper. Section 1200 exists and is titled Interruption on Enstar's own page, Enstar confirms only that phasing is by customer class with human needs highest, and the ORDER below that reaches the public solely through Kenai's mayor relaying a meeting. Then at scoring the AI line died too. Slide 08 had read 'A data center is a large commercial and industrial customer', which carried no claim id because no source says it, and on inspection it is also the weakest inference in the deck, since a Southcentral data center buys ELECTRICITY and the route to this order runs through the power plant. It now reads 'A data center buys power, and Southcentral makes more than 70 percent of its power from gas', which is C28 and is both true and stronger. Nothing in the deck predicts a shortage. C10, the 63.7 days of cover figure, is excluded on the record and the reason is written into the storyboard. Slide 06 prints NO SAFETY VERDICT, Enstar's own refusal to forecast is the largest block on slide 04, and the mayor's account is fenced on slide 08 by open boxes, a narrower type width, a dated attribution naming Homer News, and the total absence of the word tariff on that sheet. One editorial flag for you. No.27 on August 6th ran an adjacent Enstar gas beat, 36 days back, which clears the 30 day rule but is the same lane, and neither the deck nor the caption acknowledges it.

  • The one number to repeat if asked is 7.65 of 13.0 Bcf, read September 10th.
